finding.message: src/presentation/app.ts (presentation) skips layers to import src/persistence/gateways.ts (persistence)

answer.explanation: At line 10, src/presentation/app.ts imports the `Gateways` type and the `createGateways` factory from src/persistence/gateways.ts. It uses them in three places. `createApp` takes `gateways: Gateways = createGateways()` as a default parameter (line 16). `buildApp` declares `gateways: Gateways` in its public signature (line 20). That value is then passed straight into `new WeatherService(repos, gateways)` (line 28). This makes the presentation module the composition root for persistence-level external gateways: it builds and types persistence objects itself instead of getting everything through the business layer. FF-S03 flags this because a presentation-layer file depends directly on the persistence layer and skips the business layer between them. Presentation code is then tied to how persistence is built and what its types look like, so a change to the gateway API reaches the HTTP layer. Line 11 has the same pattern with `createRepositories` from ../persistence/repositories, which suggests the whole wiring of services, repositories and gateways sits in app.ts. None of the supplied docs, ADRs or comments say this wiring is intended or allowed.

answer.explanation: At line 11, src/presentation/app.ts imports createRepositories from src/persistence/repositories.ts. It calls that function once, at line 21, inside buildApp. The resulting repos object is passed to the constructors of the business services (TeamService, PlayerService, RefereeService, FixtureService, PitchService, TableService and WeatherService, lines 22-28). In the code shown, the route handlers only call services and never touch repos directly. So app.ts is acting as the composition root: it wires persistence into business, and there is no visible data access that bypasses the business layer. Even so, the presentation module depends on the persistence module at compile time without going through business. That is the layer skip FF-S03 flags. Line 10 follows the same pattern, importing Gateways and createGateways from ../persistence/gateways, which makes presentation's coupling to persistence wider than this one edge. No documentation, ADR or comment was provided that declares an intent or an exception for this wiring, and the code contains no comment that grants it.

finding.message: src/presentation/server.ts (presentation) skips layers to import src/persistence/gateways.ts (persistence)

answer.explanation: src/presentation/server.ts is the process entry point. On line 1 it imports createGateways from the persistence layer, and on line 5 it passes the result straight into buildApp(createGateways()). It does not query data itself. It acts as a composition root: it builds the persistence gateways, hands them to the app, and then starts the daily weather check (lines 9-11) and the HTTP listener (line 13). FF-S03 flags this because a presentation-layer file imports a persistence-layer module directly and skips the layers in between. That breaks the strict layering the rule enforces, whatever the reason for the import. No docs, ADRs or comments were provided that call this file a sanctioned composition root or exempt it from layering. The only nearby comment (line 7) is about the forecast schedule. The usual fix is to move the wiring into a dedicated bootstrap or composition module outside the presentation layer, or to have an intermediate layer expose the gateway factory. Either way, presentation would no longer reference persistence directly.
